result.summary: Verdict FINDINGS at target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895 (feature/binary-config-serve-20260930). Scope: Prometheus listener config, auth exposure, labels/cardinality, correctness, bind/shutdown. 3 findings. HIGH: src/metrics.ts:70 render() is O(retained workers x events) - 5 SQL statements per historical worker, EXPLAIN shows SCAN events (no index on events(worker_id,type)) - and one unauthenticated GET /metrics blocked the shared Bun event loop for 44ms/535ms/7.7s/20.8s at 250/1000/2000/4000 retained workers, stalling MCP /health; no DELETE exists in src/store.ts so cost grows for the life of the DB. HIGH: src/serve.ts:178 metrics listener has no auth and no Host validation and binds SWARMFORGE_HOST, so SWARMFORGE_HOST=0.0.0.0 (the supported public path, token-protected MCP) publishes :9090/metrics; loopback config returned 200 for no auth, wrong bearer and Host: attacker.example.com while /health returned 401/403. LOW: src/metrics.ts:79 labels swarmforge_tokens_total with configured SWARMFORGE_MODEL_NAME, ignoring the persisted usage.model (src/coordinator.ts:546), reproduced misattribution. Bind/shutdown ordering, port rollback and team bucketing verified correct; prom-client escapes hostile label values. Tests: bun test tests/serve.test.ts 20 pass/0 fail exit 0 (Bun 1.4.2 in /tmp clone); six bounded local probes, no real provider/network. Artifacts: /workspace/.swarmforge/artifacts/review.md and findings.json.
result.details:
Reviewer workspace /workspace/repo left clean at assigned baseline 5672ead; all work in disposable clone /tmp/sfrev/target (rev-parse HEAD = target). Official Bun 1.4.2 in /tmp/bun142; lockfile untouched. No source changes.

F1 HIGH src/metrics.ts:70 (handler src/serve.ts:178-192): render() walks store.all() (no DELETE FROM anywhere in src/store.ts) and issues per-worker GROUP BY, min(ready) and per-dispatch result.received statements; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN returns SCAN events for two of them because events has only PK(id) (src/store.ts:27). Measured: 2000 retained workers -> 2100 ms and 10003 statements in-process; concurrent MCP /health latency during a scrape 44-50 ms (250), 535-562 ms (1000), 7.7-10.3 s (2000), 20.8-23.1 s (4000). Impact: MCP calls, reconciliation and turn deadlines stall; default 15 s Prometheus scraping wedges a long-lived instance. Guard gap: tests/serve.test.ts:525-560 only asserts status 200 on a near-empty DB; no cache/TTL/timeout/index. Fix: set-based aggregates, index events(worker_id,type), cache exposition for seconds, persist result timing on the dispatch row.

F2 HIGH src/serve.ts:178: handler checks only pathname; no token, no Host allowlist (contrast src/http.ts:11-28); SWARMFORGE_HOST is the sole bind variable for both listeners and src/config.ts:142-150 only requires differing ports. Reproduced on loopback+token: /metrics 200 with no auth, 200 with wrong bearer, 200 with hostile Host, vs /health 401/403. With SWARMFORGE_HOST=0.0.0.0 metrics answered 200 on non-loopback 172.17.0.1 while /health gave 403; payload leaks allowlisted team IDs, model name, state counts, token volumes. Docs say 'protect externally', unachievable with one host variable. Fix: add SWARMFORGE_METRICS_HOST default 127.0.0.1 and reuse the Host allowlist / optional token in the metrics handler.

F3 LOW src/metrics.ts:79: model label always the configured name although src/coordinator.ts:546 persists m.model; usage rows with model some-other-model-9000 exported as model="qwen"; store.tokens() lacks GROUP BY model.

No findings: team->other bucketing and cardinality bounds, prom-client label escaping (no exposition injection), counter semantics, listener release order/idempotency and both occupied-port rollback paths, metrics served during provisioning.

Limitations: container-local timings; non-loopback check on docker0 only; F3 seeded directly; settings parsing and MCP status output not exhaustively reviewed. Probes in /tmp/sfrev/probe, logs in /workspace/.swarmforge/logs.

result.followup_reason: Two HIGH findings are actionable: src/serve.ts:178 should add a dedicated metrics bind host plus the existing Host/token guards, and src/metrics.ts:70 should replace the per-worker loop with set-based aggregates (index events(worker_id,type)) and cache the exposition to stop a single scrape from blocking the event loop for tens of seconds.
